```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(cache = TRUE)
```

# Introduction

This template guides you in building a report-generation workflow for an electronic package.
If you render this workflow in your daily working environment, the report is generated directly.
If this file is used as input for the `exportTLFWorkflowToEPackage` function, the `.Rmd` file is converted to a workflow `.R` script, and all required inputs are copied to the ePackage folder (see also the Electronic Package vignette).

This workflow is interpreted by a script, so the file content and structure must follow these rules:

Each chunk name has a suffix that determines how the export script handles the chunk:

- `-copy`: The code is copied to the final workflow script as is.
- `-eval`: The code is evaluated, and the evaluated result is used during export.
- `-replace`: The code is ignored and replaced with default code.
- `-QC`: These chunks are placeholders for user-defined checks; their code is ignored by the export script.

Do not delete any template chunk (except `-QC` chunks), or `exportTLFWorkflowToEPackage` will fail.

The script uses only predefined template chunks. You can add additional chunks (for example, for debugging or QC), but these chunks are not included in the exported workflow script.

Each template chunk has dedicated conversion logic. Please read the description above each chunk carefully.


# Report Generation Workflow

## Initialization

### Libraries

This chunk is copied as is by `exportTLFWorkflowToEPackage`; please list any additional libraries here:

```{r libraries-copy}
library(ospsuite.reportingframework)

```

### Custom functions

If you want to source custom functions, add each file name (including relative path) to `pathsCustomfunctions` in the `pathsCustomfunctions-eval` chunk.
`exportTLFWorkflowToEPackage` evaluates this chunk, copies those function files to the electronic package, and adds corresponding `source(...)` lines to the final workflow script.
The original code of these chunks is not included in the final workflow script.

```{r pathsCustomfunctions-eval}
pathsCustomfunctions <- c()
```

```{r customfunctions-replace}
if (length(pathsCustomfunctions) > 0)
  lapply(pathsCustomfunctions,source)
```


### Workflow options

Workflow options are set via the `QCpassed` environment variable. The default is `FALSE`.
Do not edit this chunk. Changes are ignored by `exportTLFWorkflowToEPackage`.

```{r workflowOptions-replace}
setWorkflowOptions(isValidRun = getQCpassedEnvironmentVariable())
```

### Set up project structure

This chunk is replaced with code that generates `projectConfiguration` via `importWorkflow`.
This function builds a new project directory using input files stored in the electronic package.
Changes in the chunk below will be ignored by the `exportTLFWorkflowToEPackage` function.

```{r projectConfiguration-replace}
projectConfiguration <-
  ospsuite.reportingframework::createProjectConfiguration(
    path =  file.path("ProjectConfiguration.xlsx"))

# initialize the logging
setLogPath(
  logFolder = file.path(projectConfiguration$outputFolder, "logs"),
  logFileName = "workflow.log"
)

```


## Load observed data

The workflow export script evaluates the chunks `dataObserved-eval` and `dataObservedPK-eval`.
If `dataObserved` (or `dataObservedPK`) is `NULL`, the corresponding import is skipped.
Use `dataObserved <- NULL` (or `dataObservedPK <- NULL`) when no data is available.

If a table is not `NULL`, the evaluated `data.table` object (`dataObserved` or `dataObservedPK`) is exported as `.csv` to the electronic package, and corresponding data-import configuration tables are exported as well.
The original chunk code is not included in the final workflow script. You can therefore add preprocessing logic (for example, filtering) before export.
The final workflow script imports the required data with `readObservedDataByDictionary` without further adjustments.
`spreadData` is set to `FALSE`, so configuration tables are not modified.

Ensure that `dataObserved` and `dataObservedPK` contain only workflow-relevant data in the expected format.
Use `validateObservedData` to check the format.
Suggested checks are provided in `-QC` chunks. These chunks are ignored by the export script.
See also `check-usedData-QC` in section "Create output plots".

```{r dataObserved-eval}
# use this line if you have no observed time profile data
dataObserved <- NULL

# use the code below if you have observed time profile data
dataObserved <- readObservedDataByDictionary(projectConfiguration = projectConfiguration,
                                             dataClassType = 'timeprofile',
                                             fileIds = NULL,
                                             spreadData = FALSE)

# here you can add your own code to manipulate and clean the data if necessary

```


```{r observedTimeprofiles-QC}
# check the format
validateObservedData(dataObserved,dataClassType = 'timeprofile')

# add quality checks to ensure data contains only the required records.
print(names(dataObserved))

print(dataObserved[,.(N = .N,
                      xmin = min(xValues),
                      xmax = max(xValues),
                      ymin = min(yValues),
                      ymax = max(yValues)),
                   by = c('group','outputPathId')])

```


```{r dataObservedPK-eval}
# use this line if you have no observed PK parameter data
dataObservedPK <- NULL

# use the code below if you have observed PK parameter data
dataObservedPK <- readObservedDataByDictionary(projectConfiguration = projectConfiguration,
                                             dataClassType = 'pkParameter',
                                             fileIds = NULL,
                                             spreadData = FALSE)
# here you can add your own code to manipulate and clean the data if necessary
```


```{r observedPKParameter-QC}
# check the format
validateObservedData(dataObservedPK,dataClassType = 'pkParameter')

# add quality checks to ensure data contains only the required records.
print(names(dataObservedPK))

```

### Optional: load numeric values

The workflow export script evaluates `numericValues-eval` during export.
If `numericValues` is not `NULL`, the evaluated table is exported as a CSV file into the electronic package and reloaded in the final workflow script from that file.
In this authoring chunk, you can still use `readObservedDataByDictionary` to build `numericValues` from your working configuration.
This means you can keep preprocessing logic here, and the exported workflow remains reproducible.

```{r numericValues-eval}
# use this line if you have no numeric values data
numericValues <- NULL

# use the code below if you have numeric values data
numericValues <- readObservedDataByDictionary(projectConfiguration = projectConfiguration,
                                              dataClassType = 'numericValues',
                                              fileIds = NULL,
                                              spreadData = FALSE)

# example: extract one numeric value for reuse in workflow code
# doseMg <- getNumericValue(numericValues, variableName = 'Dose', expectedUnit = 'mg')
```

```{r numericValues-QC}
# optional quality checks for numeric values
if (!is.null(numericValues)) {
  print(names(numericValues))
  print(numericValues)
}
```

## Load simulation results

These code chunks are copied as is to the final workflow script.
The first chunk is evaluated to obtain the scenario list from `scenarioNames`.
Configuration tables are exported accordingly, so make sure `scenarioNames` includes all scenarios required by the workflow.

```{r scenarioNames-eval}
scenarioNames = c()
```

```{r loadResults-copy}

# It is assumed that all required scenarios were simulated in previous workflow started in same project directory.
scenarioResults <- loadScenarioResultsToFramework(projectConfiguration = projectConfiguration,
                          scenarioNames = scenarioNames)

pkParameterDT <- loadPKParameter(projectConfiguration = projectConfiguration,
                                 scenarioListOrResult = scenarioResults)
```

## Create output plots

This chunk is copied as is to the final workflow script. Adjust the code to your needs.
The script searches the chunk text for expressions like `configTableSheet = "..."` and updates plot configuration accordingly.
Please make sure all required plot configuration sheets are referenced this way.

```{r runPlot-copy}
# set graphic
ggplot2::theme_set(theme_osp())
options(knitr.kable.NA = '')

runPlotTheme <- ggplot2::theme(
  legend.position = "top",
  legend.title = ggplot2::element_blank()
)

# timeprofiles
runPlot(
  nameOfplotFunction = "plotTimeProfiles",
  projectConfiguration = projectConfiguration,
  configTableSheet = "TimeProfiles",
  theme = runPlotTheme,
  inputs = list(
    dataObserved = dataObserved,
    scenarioResults = scenarioResults
  )
)

```


The function `plotTimeProfiles` supports the input variable `checkForUnusedData`.
This switches the mode to `suppressExport` and returns `unusedDataRows` in the result list.
To verify that `dataObserved` contains only data used in plots, adapt the code below and inspect `plotList$unusedDataRows`.

```{r check-usedData-QC}

plotList <-
    runPlot(
      nameOfplotFunction = "plotTimeProfiles",
  configTableSheet = "TimeProfiles",
      projectConfiguration = projectConfiguration,
      checkForUnusedData = TRUE,
      theme = runPlotTheme,
      inputs = list(
        scenarioResults = scenarioResults,
        dataObserved = dataObserved
      )
    )

  expect_equal(nrow(plotList$unusedDataRows), expected = 0)


```

## Finalize workflow

Each workflow ends with the code of the chunk below. Changes will be ignored.

```{r finalize-replace}
addMessageToLog("finalize workflow")

# save session information including loaded packages and R version to a log file
saveSessionInfo(fileName = paste0("w", wfIdentifier, "_sessionInfo.log"))
```
